tagline: From a found diamond to a mountain gap.
intro: Out of Peterstown, across Rich Creek from Virginia, the backway takes one-lane roads, some paved and some gravel, toward Gap Mills. The farms along them were carved out of the mountain valleys by settlers who lived apart from the rest of the county, by choice or by economic necessity.

Over all of it stands Peters Mountain, a ridge forty miles long, and the backway gives access to the Allegheny and Appalachian trails. Gap Mills takes its name from the gap in the adjacent mountain and two gristmills that once stood there; the mills survive in the name.

moments.title: Peterstown
moments.text: Grover Jones and his son William, known as Punch, found the 34.48-carat Jones Diamond here in 1928.

moments.title: Gap Mills
moments.text: The village dates from 1775, but the first recorded English expedition reached the area in 1671, sent by Abraham Wood of Fort Henry.

practical: Every road is one lane, paved or gravel; RVs are not recommended because the roads are narrow.
